title: Tenancy Stability Controller (TSC) - guarded gating, headroom rebalancer, and tenant quarantine PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Introduce a Tenancy Stability Controller (TSC) for Dedicated capacity that centrally enforces gating policies, maintains minimum headroom, and offers a quarantine path for noisy tenants to protect tail latency and throughput SLOs across pools.
context: As Dedicated customers scale, noisy tenants and unpredictable burst patterns occasionally consume disproportionate reserved resources which leads to tail latency violations for other tenants sharing a pool. Current mitigations are ad-hoc (manual ticketing, coarse preemption, broad throttles) and do not provide observability nor safe automated remediation. We need a coherent controller that operates at allocation time and at runtime to keep pools healthy while preserving customer SLAs and predictable economics.
problem_statement: 1) Pools lack dynamic, enforceable headroom and gating enforcement which causes SLO regressions during correlated bursts. 2) On-call escalations and manual preemption are labor-intensive and slow. 3) There is insufficient telemetry surfaced to customers and operators for noisy-tenant detection and remediation. 4) Automated protection must respect reserved commitments and avoid over-eager evictions.
goals: Provide an automated controller that keeps a configurable minimum headroom percentage per pool (e.g., 10%) and rebalances reservations when capacity drift is detected.
Offer a tenant quarantine mode that moves or rate-limits offending tenants into an isolated soft-slice without evicting them outright, preserving committed throughput but capping burst impact.
Expose clear telemetry and alerted signals for noisy tenant detection, quarantine events, and headroom pressure to both ops and customers via Console and API.
Support policy-driven gating at request admission to prevent single-tenant spikes from consuming >X% of active burst headroom.
Enable gradual rollout with canary on a subset of pools and an operator-revert path; maintain an audit trail for all automated actions.
Minimize customer-visible negative impact: committed reserved slowdowns should be avoided; best-effort burst behavior may be limited during incidents but documented and predictable.
success_metrics: Reduce incidents where pool tail latency (p99 generation latency) exceeds SLO by >2x during peak bursts by 70% within two months of rollout.
Decrease number of manual preemption tickets related to noisy tenants by 80% in the first quarter after GA.
Percentage of pools with headroom maintained above configured thresholds >= 95% during business hours in steady state.
Time-to-detect noisy tenant (operator-visible signal) under 5 minutes in 90% of noisy burst cases.
No customer with active reserved contract should experience >10% sustained request throttling for more than 10 minutes due to TSC actions (target: 98% of customers remain under this bound).
Console/Alert coverage: at least three templated alerts for headroom_pressure, quarantine_triggered, and gate_enforced in default dashboards.
Feature telemetry does not increase token billing overhead by more than 2% (budget constraint for instrumentation).
non_goals: This PRD does not replace long-term multi-cluster global autoscaling—TSC operates within pool boundaries.
TSC will not change pricing or billing behavior for reserved customers in this milestone.
This work will not implement hardware-level preemption (e.g., GPU eviction) in phase 1.
No changes to customer identity/entitlement model beyond tagging tenants for quarantine eligibility.
We will not provide an automated pushback mechanism to end-users outside Redwood (i.e., customer app-level rate limiting) in phase 1.
TSC will not re-architect request routing across regions; cross-region routing is out of scope for this release.
user_personas: Platform Operator: needs reliable, automated protection to keep pools within SLOs and reduce oncall load.
SRE/Oncall: needs clear signals and playbook steps for quarantines and policy tuning.
Dedicated Tenant Admin: expects transparency, minimal impact to committed capacity, and ability to appeal or request exemption.
Product Manager/Engineering: needs a predictable contract with other teams for rollout windows, telemetry and gating defaults.
Solutions Engineer / Customer Success: needs documentation, configurable knobs, and communication templates for impacted customers.
requirements: R1 - Headroom Enforcement: Pools must maintain a configurable minimum headroom percentage (default 10%) computed from active pool capacity and reserved allocations.

R2 - Headroom Rebalancer: When headroom falls below threshold for >2m, controller should attempt non-disruptive rebalancing by (a) borrowing from idle ephemeral capacity, (b) moving soft-burst allocations within tenant cohorts, or (c) initiating controlled canary prewarming of standby nodes. All actions must be auditable.

R3 - Noisy Tenant Detector: Implement heuristic scoring using burst rate, steady-state consumption, and token-per-second variance. Score calculation to run every 60s and flag tenants that exceed noise_threshold for 3 consecutive intervals.

R4 - Quarantine Mode: For flagged tenants, apply a quarantine policy that (a) reduces best-effort burst headroom to a capped value, (b) optionally rate-limits new burst requests, and (c) isolates KV/prefix cache effects where applicable. Quarantine should have TTL and operator/customer override paths.

R5 - Admission Gating: Enforce per-tenant gating that denies or soft-blocks requests that would consume >configured_percent_of_headroom in one request. Gating decisions must return structured reasons and include suggested remediation messages.

R6 - Telemetry & Alerts: Emit events for headroom_pressure, noisy_tenant_detected, quarantine_started/stopped, rebalancer_action. Events must include pool_id, tenant_id, snapshot metrics, and controller_decision_id.
R7 - Console UI: Add a pool-level 'Stability' tab with headroom graph, quarantine list, recent controller actions, and a toggle to enable/disable automatic quarantine for that pool.
R8 - Audit Trail & Appeals: Allow tenant admins to submit appeal requests with auto-link to original controller_decision_id. Appeals must be tracked and visible to ops and the tenant in Console.
R9 - Canary Rollout: The controller must support staged rollout flags by pool and provide a dry-run mode that surfaces decisions as warnings but does not enact them.
R10 - Safety Constraints: Controller must never reduce guaranteed reserved throughput below contracted minimum; only best-effort allocations may be limited or moved.

R11 - API: Provide REST endpoints for listing TSC decisions, querying per-tenant status, and applying manual overrides. API must support pagination and filtering by pool, tenant, decision type, and time range.
R12 - Operational Runbooks: Provide playbook for triage, rollback, and customer communication for quarantine events.
R13 - Metrics Budget: Telemetry should adhere to metrics budget and be configurable per-org to avoid runaway costs.
R14 - Data Retention: Controller events must be retained for 90 days for audit purposes (configurable per enterprise contract).
ux_flow: Operator opens Console -> navigates to Dedicated pool -> Stability tab shows current headroom and active quarantines -> TSC dry-run toggle off/on -> operator views proposed actions -> operator approves or allows automatic enforcement. Tenant admin sees quarantine notice in tenant Console with appeal link and expected ETA for review.
api_spec: GET /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/tsc/decisions?cursor=&limit= -> returns list of decisions (decision_id, timestamp, type, summary, status)
GET /v1/dedicated/tenants/{tenant_id}/tsc/status -> returns current quarantine state, score, last_action_time
POST /v1/dedicated/decisions/{decision_id}/override -> body: {action: 'revoke'|'extend'|'escalate', reason: string} -> creates audit entry
POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/tsc/dry_run -> body: {enabled: true|false} -> toggles dry-run for pool
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Headroom Enforcement implemented and configurable per pool with UI control; default set to 10% and visible graphs displaying target vs actual.
AC2: Noisy tenant detector running in dry-run mode on canary pools for at least 2 weeks with validated detection precision >= 75% and recall >= 60% against annotated incidents.
AC3: Quarantine mode available and can be applied automatically or manually; when applied in a test pool, burst-related tail latency for co-tenants improves by >=40% on average compared to baseline.

AC4: Controller respects reserved guarantees: automated actions must not reduce contracted reserved throughput; unit tests and an integration test asserting reserved requests always pass under stress.
AC5: API endpoints exist and pass contract tests (pagination/filtering/override) and instrumentation events emitted for every decision.
AC6: Console Stability tab implemented with operator controls and tenant appeal flow; UX passes product/design review and basic accessibility checks.
AC7: Alerts for headroom_pressure, quarantine_started are wired to PagerDuty/Slack with escape hatches; first-run alerting template documented in runbook.
AC8: Rollout plan executed: dry-run -> 10% pools -> 30% -> gradual to 100% with no more than 1 rollback required during canary (rollback criteria defined in runbook).
AC9: Documentation and runbook published and linked; security review completed and KMS/HSM interactions validated where audit records are encrypted.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dry-run): Implement TSC in dry-run on 5 non-production pools and surface decisions in Console for 2 weeks. Phase 1 (canary): Enable enforcement for 10% low-risk production pools with on-call monitoring and 24/7 pager coverage for first 72 hours. Phase 2 (expanded): 30% pools with longer observation window and customer opt-in for quarantine. Phase 3 (GA): Full rollout with default headroom enabled and org-level configuration. Each phase includes a rollback playbook and a post-mortem window.
open_questions: Q1: Exact noise scoring algorithm and threshold—use ML classifier vs rule-based heuristics? (engineering to prototype both in spike).
Q2: Default headroom percentage for different pool sizes—should we have size-tiered defaults (e.g., 5% for very large pools, 15% for small pools)?
Q3: How to bill/communicate the effect of quarantine to customers with strict reserved contracts (legal/commercial review required).
Q4: What is the allowable frequency of automated rebalancer moves before we require explicit human approval?
Q5: If quarantine is applied, do we automatically notify only tenant admins or also workspace owners and customer success? What's the communication cadence?
dependencies: D1: Console team - Stability tab and appeal UI components
D2: Serving runtime - ability to apply per-tenant soft rate limits and per-request gating hooks
D3: Observability - event pipeline and retention policy updates for TSC events
D4: Billing/Legal - review for quarantine impacts on committed contracts
D5: Auth/Entitlements - tenant tagging and override permissions
D6: Oncall - 24/7 coverage during canary windows
risks_mitigation: Risk: Overzealous quarantine causes customer dissatisfaction -> Mitigation: start in dry-run, require multi-interval confirmation, provide immediate appeals and human-in-loop override.
Risk: Controller interferes with reserved guarantees -> Mitigation: enforce safety constraint R10 in code plus integration tests and contract checks.
Risk: Telemetry volume growth -> Mitigation: metrics budget, sampling, and configurable telemetry per-org.
Risk: False positives in detection -> Mitigation: conservative defaults, multi-signal confirmation, and operator notification before enforcement in early rollout.
Risk: Legal/commercial pushback -> Mitigation: early engagement with Billing and CSM teams and opt-in paths for sensitive contracts.
